title: TE Daniel R. Morse v. Covenant Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC directed Presbytery to erase Morse and Crenshaw from its rolls under BCO 38-3 and to erase Grace Presbyterian Church after its congregational withdrawal. Grace’s three complaints were abandoned and deemed moot. The SJC nevertheless opined that recording a protest under BCO 45-5 is not subject to complaint.
first_summary: The SJC held that Morse and Crenshaw could not resign unilaterally and that joining another evangelical church required their removal under BCO 38-3. Grace Church could withdraw by congregational vote without notifying Presbytery. Its complaints were moot, and recording a protest was not subject to complaint under BCO 45-5.
summary: On Covenant Presbytery’s mixed BCO 41 reference, the SJC held that ministers Morse and Crenshaw could not resign unilaterally; joining another evangelical church invoked BCO 38-3, requiring their names erased, with notice that they were in good standing and faced no pending charges. Grace Church’s withdrawal required a congregational vote, not notice to Presbytery, so its name also was to be erased. Grace had abandoned its complaints, rendering them moot; the SJC nevertheless opined that recording a protest is insulated from complaint by BCO 45-5.

sources.supports: Case identity, jurisdiction, dispositions, reasoning, instructions, and 23-0 approval.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: SJC case 91-3; the Commission accepted the mixed reference and approved the disposition 23-0 (printed pp. 154, 157, 159; lines 14–18, 93–120, 195–199).
evidence_notes.dispute: The reference asked how to treat ministers who purported to resign and joined another church, whether congregational withdrawal required notice, and whether receiving a protest was complainable (printed p. 156; lines 85–92).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: BCO 38-3 required erasing the ministers; congregational withdrawal required only a duly called vote; the complaints were abandoned and moot; BCO 45-5 made receipt of protests final (printed pp. 157–159; lines 122–128, 132–193).
evidence_notes.qualifications: Issues 1–2 were largely nonjudicial but accepted with judicial issue 3 because they were intertwined. A records-review exception had earlier taken the contrary view on complainability (printed pp. 156–157; lines 79–120).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference; the Hopper matter appearing after the vote is unrelated (printed p. 160; lines 201–203).

source_limits: The supplied case text is the sole authority. It records both abandonment/mootness and a merits opinion on complainability, but no separate relief on the abandoned complaints.

score_reasons.decision: States the roll-removal instructions and the abandonment/mootness of all complaints.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Gives the controlling BCO provisions and factual predicates.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the distinction between congregational voting and notice, and BCO 45-5’s specific limitation on complaints.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the formal abandonment judgment from the SJC’s additional merits opinion and the contrary records-review exception.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only details needed to explain the rulings and practical consequences.

verification_notes: Rechecked the jurisdiction, issue-by-issue disposition, roll-removal instructions, and 23-0 vote. The final summary corrects the first by stating that the complaints were both abandoned and moot and by characterizing the BCO 45-5 discussion as an additional opinion rather than relief on the abandoned complaints.
